audit.why: 47.75% over 1378 games, HARD 8/10. Irelia owns lane through resets and mobility; Mundo's only stage is two HP items, which is exactly what the packet levelChart says.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[4..6] and phases[4..6].side all read 'Skill' while the prose on those rows says Level 6 is hers, first item is hers, and only the two-item stage is yours.
audit.why: Nothing about level 6 favours Mundo here — Vanguard's Edge is a 950-range mark plus a wall — and her first item beats his. The flip is real but late.
audit.corrected: Level 6 -> Irelia (3/10), First item -> Irelia (4/10), 2+ items -> Dr. Mundo (7/10) as one atomic group, with phases[4].why and phases[5].why rewritten to stop promising a flip at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabrications ran through this matchup. (a) 'on-hit true damage' and 'her passive shreds your resists' — Ionian Fervor grants stacking bonus attack speed and, at max stacks, bonus damage on hit; no true damage and no resistance shred appear anywhere in her kit. (b) 'R Vanguard's Edge disarms' — Riot's text says it damages, marks, and then forms a wall that damages and slows enemies who walk through it; there is no disarm. (c) The decisive interaction was missing entirely: Mundo's passive resists the FIRST immobilizing effect, so her Flawless Duet stun is absorbed and drops a healing cannister. Also unstated: Bladesurge heals her on every strike and refreshes on Marked or dying targets, so leaving her a low minion is what feeds the reset chain.
audit.why: A Mundo told 'she shreds your resists' builds the wrong item; a Mundo told 'she disarms you' fights the wrong way. The true version is: deny reset fodder, bring anti-heal, and remember your passive eats one stun — the second one is the one that kills you.
audit.corrected: Passive restated as Ionian Fervor attack-speed stacking; R restated as mark plus damaging, slowing wall (and paired with 'you have no dash, hold Flash for the wall'); passive-eats-first-stun and Bladesurge anti-heal written into spikes, phases, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Flawless Duet given as a flat '18s' in breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].
audit.why: It is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 — never 18 at any rank, and at rank 5 it is a 10s stun, which changes how long the 'safe' window actually is.

audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance's damage reduction was never mentioned.
audit.why: She takes reduced physical damage while charging W — feeding autos and your E into the charge is the worst moment to trade.
audit.corrected: Left for a future pass; recorded here rather than forced into an unrelated field.
